August 2009 ## Cautious talk on “recovery” prospects - Following a 26.7% slump in world consumption in Q1 2009 to 1.8mt, our preliminary assessment of global demand in Q2 is a 20.4% y-o-y decline to 2.0mt. Although it is encouraging that this does show a sequential quarterly improvement of 8.8% it is far too early to be talking of a general “recovery”. CRU believes all we have seen is a limited restocking surge, triggered by the increase in copper prices, ahead of longer than usual downtime and extended shutdowns through the summer. - Asia is on the leading edge of these gains, with encouraging signs to be seen in all product segments, but particularly so in sheet and strip. ACR tube offtake has also strengthened with the arrival of the hot Asian summer with one leading Chinese mill reportedly increasing its July output by 9% compared to June. Alloy rod markets have been generally slower to increase though South Korea has surprised on the upside in June. But in Europe and North America there is little or no good news to be seen with consumption volumes flat or slightly below those achieved in Q1. |Consumptio

#### **Copper tube production in China appeared to have reach bottom** 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 12 **August 2009** Copper and copper alloy mill products www.crumonitor.com # Plate, sheet, strip and foil ### North East Asian flat rolled output holds steady in Q2 North East Asian production looks to have bottomed out, with Q2 flat rolled products volumes up on Q1 although still well down y-o-y. Underlying recovery is still weak with much of the upturn attributable to restocking of depleted inventories. **Japan's** output of rolled copper product in June was a seasonally adjusted 56,775t , up 17.6% from May, but down 29.6% from a year ago, according to preliminary data from the **Japan Copper and Brass Association** on 24th July. The three leading Japanese rolled copper makers all plan to cut flat rolled production by an average of 32% in the first half of fiscal 2009, starting April (see _Industry news_ for details). **Sumitomo Metal and Mining** also expects to cut total output for fiscal 2009 by 9.1% y-o-y to 16,800t. **South Korean** production of copper plate and strip in June was flat m-o-m at 15,300t, a y-o-y decline of 8.0%. In T **aiwan** , production of copper plate, sheet and strip in March increased by 10.7% m- o-m to 23,260t. This was a fall of 20.5% y-o-y. ### Japan focuses on high value-add, but when will China? As China has taken a larger share of production of the more commoditised flat rolled products, so manufacturers elsewhere continue to shift to production of more high-value add products. Currently, in Japan, **Mitsui Mining and Smelting** is investing ¥2b to increase production capacity for 1-5 micron copper foil at its Ageo plant from 450,000 to 600,000m2 by the end of August. The company aims to have output of 1m m2 by 2011. **Furukawa Electric** began producing 3-micron foil last year at its Nikko factory and has started shipping samples of 1-2 micron foil. It plans to increase output capacity to 50,000-60,000m2 by next March, and to 100,000m2 by March 2011. **Nippon Mining & Metals Co. Ltd** also plans to start shipping copper foil for in-vehicle lithium-i

on batteries to customers in 2011. However, as China‟s semis-manufacturing industry matures, so it will start to produce products of increasing technical sophistication that will challenge that of Japanese fabricators. **Fujian Zijin Copper Co. Ltd.** is reported to have carried out successful trial production in July of 10-micron copper foil (with thickness tolerance of 0.1 micron). This is the thinnest so far produced in China. Zijin Copper has been working to achieve this target since opening its 390m yuan (US$57m) copper plate and strip line in 2007. ### Europe and North America: still cautious on prospects In Western Europe, copper flat rolled products fell again in the second quarter, down 16% on Q1. This was largely due to much weaker production by **KME** , whose copper alloys semis output fell by 33.6% y- o-y in Q2 2009 and also weakened against the first quarter. However, Q2 West European copper alloy flat rolled product volumes appear to have stabilised against Q1, up 2%. It was a similar story in North America, where Q2 alloy flat rolled products output was down 18% on Q1. Demand was reported to have picked up before the summer, but this may partly have been down to increased orders due to longer than normal summer shutdowns. Although the destocking phase looks to have ended, no speedy recovery is anticipated. Construction, automotive and manufacturing demand remains weak in both regions (see _Economic indicators_ ). Indeed, in some cases end-user demand will be permanently lower. ### New anti-bacterial products released in USA In the USA, **PMX Industries** has released the first Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) registered antibacterial materials that are available for immediate sale. This is a range of anti-bacterial copper alloy products called MicroGuard. Applications for which the materials are approved are touch surfaces in hospitals, schools, commercial buildings and homes. **Jiangxi Copper** , a major semis producer said that it has started to receive tube orders from air conditioner producers in early July, which was out of its expectation as Q3 had always been a weak quarter for the industry. Tube producer **Yantai Penghui** said its production in July was up 10% from June. The three major Chinese air-conditioner producers have all experienced significant improvement in unit sales. We estimate Q2 Chinese copper tube consumption increased by 15% from Q1 and the trend could continue for Q3 as long as the weather stays warm. 

### Q2 US tube production ended falling trend 

North American tube production has stopped falling in Q2, rising to 94,000t from 92,000t in Q1. Most of the increase came from the US.  The US Census Bureau reported that orders for construction materials and supplies increased 1.4% in June versus May. **Mueller Industries** announced its Q2 net sales of US$367.8m, compared with US$753.5m a year ago.  US$146M of the decline in net sales was attributed to lower selling prices in its plumbing and refrigeration segment.  However, the company was pleased to be profitable after making a loss in Q1 and believes the US construction industry „is at, or near, a bottom‟. 

### Western European demand stabilised in Q2 

We estimate Western European copper tube production for the second quarter of 2009 was 97,000t, 25% lower than the same period last year.  Regional production volumes in the first six months of the year were still 24% below the year-ago levels while consumption for the same period was 21% lower than a year ago.  CRU understands that the industry saw slight improvements in demand at the end of the quarter but most market participants say they do not believe in a rapid recovery. 

Finland-based **Luvata** said that the destocking period in the supply chain is over but it does not anticipate a significant pick-up in the market until mid-2010.  It predicted that Europe will be the last region to recover, after Asia followed by North America. **KME** announced that its H1 output declined 30% y-o-y, primarily due to low demand from weak Western European construction markets where most of its key products are consumed.  However, CRU believes that the Italian market has actually experienced a slight improvement with Q2 demand increasing 12% on Q1.  KME also reported consolidated sales for H1 of €898.5m (US$1.3b) compared to €1.6b (US$2.3b) for the same period last year.  While actively restructuring, the company has also lodged an appeal to the European Court of Justice in July against the judgement regarding its participation in anticompetitive agreements in the industrial copper tube market. 

On the other hand, some improvements in copper tube orders have been experienced between June 2009 and now. **Wieland-Werke** said that it is not having extended holidays in the summer and it believes that it has reached the bottom during Q2 this year. The company said

Although there was a small sequential quarterly gain of 3% from 597kt in Q1 to 614kt in Q2, on a shipping days basis there was probably no underlying increase. Comparing y-o-y, volumes in Q2 were down 22%, while those for H1 were 23% lower. It would certainly be premature to judge that the worst is passed, as with extended mill shutdowns now underway in Europe and North America, this year‟s quarterly lows could be re-tested this summer. ### US volumes still very weak, but spreads widen American brass rod output fell from 44,500t in Q1 to 43,300t in Q2. The second quarter volumes equated to a 41.6% y-o-y decline from 2008 levels, which were themselves the lowest yearly total for US shipments since 1982. **Mueller Industries** , in its recently released Q2 financial results attributed 72% of its US dollar sales decline in its OEM business segment to redu

ced volumes.  However, its cost of goods sold also contracted sharply due to reduced volumes, lower raw material costs, and lower conversion costs as a result of weaker energy prices and headcount reductions.  Operating income dropped from US$19.0m to US$8.1m, but this was aided by improved unit spreads in its brass rod operations (Port Huron and Belding).  The magnitude of the decline in the US copper and brass building products business (plumbing and OEM products) has been such that Mueller Industries‟ total employee headcount total has shrunk by 25% in twelve months from 4,739 in June 2008 to 3,566 in June 2009. 

### Italy is the bell weather of European production and sales 

With Italy accounting for around half of West European brass rod output and sales, trends in this national market are highly reflective of conditions across the continent.  Recently released Q1 industry production data from **ASSOMET** confirmed a 37.5% collapse in output.  We believe that little has changed during the second quarter, and in fact have deteriorated a little further. **KME** recently reported a 33% y-o-y fall in its Q2 semis output to 104kt from 156kt a year-earlier, compared to a 28% y-o-y fall from 157kt to 114kt in Q1 2009.  Brass rod is amongst those products being hardest hit.  Only very recently has KME reportedly seen “ _some signs of stabilisation, even at very low levels_ .”  But even so “… _the general climate is still one of uncertainty and fears that the stimulus to output deriving from the need to rebuild inventories will not be enough to launch a consolidated process of recovery._ ” 

### Asian markets are through the worst of the recession 

The clearest signs of optimism are to be found across Asia.  Different economies are lesser or further through the recession trough and are experiencing different rates of recovery from recent lows.  Japan is furthest behind, but even here there have been some modest gains through the second quarter.  Output fell to a low of 10,000 t in March as consumers destocked at the end of the financial year, but since then some restocking has emerged with output rising progressively to reach 12,500 t in June.  However, this was still 30% down on the tonnage of June 2008, with demand from every end use down on last year. 

In Taiwan, output hit bottom in January with only 5,300t extruded.  But sequential gains followed over the next three months bringing production up to 8,600t, before a decline back to 7,500t in May as the recovery stuttered.  South Korea has shown an even more convincing pace and sustainability of recovery. From a low of only 10,900t in January, production has climbed steadily, though not always consecutively, up to a high of 18,800t in June.  Producer inventories are well under control and further sequential growth is probable through the third quarter. After rising in April and May, the LME copper price broke through the $5,000/t barrier at the start of June, reaching a monthly high of $5,381/t on 11th June. Late June saw a retreat, with cash prices falling to a low of $4,690/t as market participants became more cautious. Prices then started to rise again, breaching $6,200/t in early August on low trading volumes. With demand still weak, and no cutbacks in supply, prices seem to be ahead of fundamentals. Sentiment has been boosted by strong Chinese imports figures and declining stocks. In addition, prices have risen as a result of increased investor interest, as risk appetite has returned. rates.|757.4|985.1|685.2|_780.0_|_800.0_| 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 10 of 12 **August 2009** Copper and copper alloy mill products www.crumonitor.com # Industry news ### North America - Ohio-based supplier of specialty copper alloy products **Brush Engineered Materials Inc.** reported Q2 2009 sales were US$174.1m, 29% lower than the same period a year ago but an improvement of 29% from Q1. The Specialty Engineered Alloys segment reported Q2 sales of US$41.2m, compared to sales of US$83.0m a year ago. The decline in segment sales was primarily due to the effect of the severe global recession in its key markets. - **Mueller Industries** reported net sales for the second quarter ended 27 June 2009 were US$367m, compared to US$753m a year ago. The company achieved net income of US$6.0m in the second quarter versus US$27m last year. Operating income was US$14m, compared to US$47 m last year. The company said the fall in net sales was mainly down to lower copper and brass prices as well as lower sales volume in the OEM segment. - **The Copper and Brass Fabricators Council** reported US imports of brass mill products in May declined by 34.9% y-o-y to 16,034t whilst exports plummeted by 43.9% y-o-y to 7,312t. Imports of flat rolled products reached 3,110t, while exports amounted to 2,572t. Imports of tube products were 9,510t and exports 2,386t. Rods, bars and sections imports were 2,635t whilst exports 1,646t. Finally, imported alloy wire added up to 778t and exports totalled 708t. ### Europe - **Hutmen** hopes to make a profit selling the assets of the closed **Szopienice** plant. It plans to open a new copper tube production facility together with **KGHM** with the money left from the sale and after payi

ng off debts. The value of this investment is estimated at ZL100 m (US$33.8m). Hutmen is planning to build the new plant next to **KGHM's Huta Miedzi Legnica** copper mill. 

- **Luvata** said that a significant rise in demand is not anticipated until mid-2010. As a result of destocking, it has got used to operating at a lower level of stock, and therefore became more efficient in its production procedures. Luvata intends to keep operating at lower stock levels even in periods of growth. It said that demand before the summer showed some recovery signs and it is now waiting for the autumn to see whether the positive trend will continue. 

- **KME** said that its H1 output dropped 30% to 218,000t from 313,000t for the same period a year ago. Semis demand has been badly hit by the economic downturn and a slowdown in investments in new plants and machinery. However, a fall in copper prices earlier in the year helped ease substitution threats from cheaper materials. KME announced that its consolidated sales dropped 45% y-o-y to €898.5m (US$1.29b) for the first half of 2009. 

### North East Asia 







- The annual production capacity of Korean copper rolling facilities is expected to exceed 300,000t within two years, with expansions at **Poongsan** and **Lee Ku Industrial** . At present, their production capacity is close to 260,000t/y, but actual output capacity is about 240,000t/y.  Poongsan will increase its rolled copper production capacity by 23,000t by 2010 from its current 150,000t. Lee Ku Industrial reportedly plans to install additional cold-rolling facilities at its Poseung plant, though the investment period has not yet been decided. 

- Major Japanese rolled copper makers announced plans to cut their flat rolled production. **Hitachi Cable** plans to produce 15,240t in the first half FY2009, down 34% from the first half FY2008. **Dowa Metaltech** plans a 41% y-o-y cut, with brass products down 46% to 5,160t, and copper flat rolled down 39% to 10,806t. **Nippon Mining & Metals** plans a 16% y-o-y cut to 16,020t. **Sumitomo Metal Mining Brass & Copper Co. Ltd.** also expects to cut production for fiscal 2009 by 9.1% to 1,400t per month. **Furukawa Electric** plans domestic monthly output of 7m square meter electrolytic copper foil in the first half started April, 15% lower y-o-y.

### Developing Asia 









- **Haoyu Metal Material Co. Ltd.** has started constructing a RMB100m (US$14.62m) 120,000t copper processing facility in Tongliao City in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. The facility will produce copper rod, plate and wire, and production is scheduled to start by the end of August. 

- **Jinchuan Group Ltd** plans to put its 60,000t copper-nickel alloys rod project into trial production in November 2009, and commission it in March 2010, according to a company source. This will bring the company‟s total capacity for flat rolled products up to 250,000t by 2010. Products from the new project will be used in desalination, vessel manufacture, ocean engineering, coal and nuclear power, auto manufacture and military industry. 

- **Jiangxi Sanchuan Copper Co. Ltd.** started constructing its new 54,000t copper semis project in Yingtan City on 16 June. The company, which manufactures products including cable, copper rod & sheet, is investing 260 m yuan in the project.
